question: As published by El País on 13 March 2024, 60 migrants have died of hunger and thirst, among them women and children, in a boat adrift in the central Mediterranean. The survivors have said that they received no help despite the fact that planes and helicopters flew over the boat. The boat could have been the subject of an alarm by Alarm Phone. The International Organization for Migration warns that this tragedy demonstrates the widespread inadequacy of the relief system in the central Mediterranean. 1.

Can the Commission identify the nationality and owners of the planes and helicopters that the survivors saw and clarify whether the European Border and Coast Guard Agency, the Italian Coast Guard, or other European rescue and coordination mechanisms were aware of the need for assistance? Can it provide the precise date of this information?
Given the dysfunctionality of the rescue system in the Mediterranean, will the Commission propose the establishment of a European search and rescue mission as requested by Parliament on 13 July 2023?
answer: The Commission is aware that on 13 March 2024 two vessels in distress were rescued and that reportedly one of them carried survivors who had been drifting at sea for days.

However, the Commission does not have access to the operational information referred to in the first question, which only the European Border and Coast Guard Agency, the Italian Coast Guard, or other European rescue and coordination mechanisms, such as the national Rescue Coordination Centres may be able to provide.

Search and Rescue (SAR) is a national responsibility of Member States (1), where the applicable legal framework mainly derives from international law. The Commission has no competence to either launch or coordinate a rescue operation, nor to identify a safe place for disembarkation.

Nevertheless, the Commission remains committed to promoting and supporting enhanced cooperation between Member States to better coordinate SAR and save lives at sea, including in the context of the European Contact Group on Search and Rescue.

International Convention on Maritime Search and Rescue (SAR Convention), 1979: https://treaties.un.org/doc/Publication/UNTS/Volume%201405/volume1405-I-23489-English.pdf; and International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS), 1974: https://treaties.un.org/doc/Publication/UNTS/Volume %201226/volume-1226-I-18961-English.pdf
